Noailles was further terrified by the Council of Embrun and by the King's authority in defending its acts. In 1727, several bishops had gathered at Embrun to defeat the monstrous errors that were being scattered everywhere by the schismatics and to settle the disturbances they had incited. Furthermore, there were two primary acts: the condemnation of Father Courrayer, from the monastery of Saint Genevieve, along with his book against the real presence of Christ in the Eucharist, who set out for England to carry out the system of Dupin and distinguished himself there with other writings regarding the ordinations of Anglican bishops; and second, the sentence passed on September 20th against Soanen, the Bishop of Senez. A certain pastoral Instruction had appeared under his name, teeming with infamous errors of every kind, and in which, as much as Quesnel’s work was commended, the Bull condemning it was prostituted as worthy of all execration. But before he entered the city, he ordered it to be announced to those gathered that he would never recognize them as judges.
